name: Li fractional CO₂ laser–sham trial
question: Does fractional carbon dioxide vaginal laser improve postmenopausal vaginal symptoms more than sham treatment?

design.population: Postmenopausal women seeking treatment for vaginal dyspareunia, burning, itching, or dryness at a Sydney tertiary referral hospital.
design.locator: PMC full text, Abstract and Methods

verdictNote: Neither prespecified symptom measure showed a significant laser advantage at 12 months.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with vaginal symptoms, three fractional microablative CO₂ laser treatments did not improve 12-month visual analog symptom severity or Vulvovaginal Symptom Questionnaire scores versus sham laser.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Li FG, Maheux-Lacroix S, Deans R, et al. "Effect of Fractional Carbon Dioxide Laser vs Sham Treatment on Symptom Severity in Women With Postmenopausal Vaginal Symptoms: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2021;326(14):1381-1389. doi:10.1001/jama.2021.14892
reports.followUpLocator: PMC full text, Abstract; Methods, Data Collection

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12 months on 0–100 VAS; mean difference, laser minus sham
results.note: Both co-primary instruments had to show statistical significance for a positive trial; a 50% reduction in each was defined as clinically important.
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract, Results; Methods, Outcomes

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12 months on 0–20 VSQ; mean difference, laser minus sham
results.note: The abstract gives the signed laser change as −3.1; the Results body prints 3.1, inconsistent with its reported difference.
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract, Results; Results, Primary Outcomes

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12 months on 0–100 VAS; mean difference, laser minus sham
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract, Results; Results, Primary Outcomes

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12 months on Assessment of Quality of Life–6D; mean difference, laser minus sham
results.note: The abstract reports difference 4.8; rounded arm changes subtract to 4.9, as printed in the Results body.
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract, Results; Results, Secondary Outcomes

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12 months on 5–25 VHI; mean difference, laser minus sham
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract, Results; Results, Secondary Outcomes

results.measure: Participants with shift among paired vaginal wall biopsies at 6 months
results.note: The paper reports no significant between-group histologic difference.
results.locator: PMC full text, Results, Secondary Outcomes

harms.label: Participants reporting at least one adverse event during treatment
harms.locator: PMC full text, Results, Adverse Events
harms.note: Reported events included transient vaginal pain or discomfort, spotting, discharge, and lower urinary tract symptoms or UTI.

harms.label: Severe adverse events
harms.note: The trial was not powered to assess uncommon complications.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule and device
delivery.value: Three SmartXide² V2LR/MonaLisa Touch treatments, 4–8 weeks apart, by laser-certified physicians.

delivery.label: Active and sham settings

values.exp: 40 W; 1000 μs dwell; 1000 μm DOT spacing; SmartStack 2, DP mode; 5.37 J/cm²
values.ctl: 0.5 W; 100 μs dwell; 2000 μm DOT spacing; SmartStack 1, SmartPulse mode; 0 J/cm²

delivery.note: The sham delivered no tissue-effect energy; visual and auditory effects and procedural maneuvers matched.

delivery.label: Topical anesthetic and masking
delivery.value: 4% topical lignocaine to the introitus for 20 minutes; plume evacuation in both arms.

delivery.label: Treatment completion and 12-month retention
delivery.locator: PMC full text, Figure 1 and Results, Participants
delivery.note: No participant discontinued treatment after randomization.
